```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

Everything between raw data and the folder REMIND reads runs through one function.

```r
pfm::pfmRun()
```

Called with no arguments in an interactive session it asks for each setting, shows
the options, and takes Enter for the default. Called with arguments it runs straight
through — so the same function serves a person at a prompt and a SLURM job.

## The five stages

| stage | what it does | writes |
|---|---|---|
| `sweep` | estimate and select: model sweep, frontier, temporal validation, sector speeds | `selected-models-psm.yml`, `frontier.rds`, … |
| `downstream` | donor assumptions, projection fan-out, coupling bound, selection bootstrap | `projection.rds`, `coupling/`, … |
| `remind` | assemble the self-contained folder REMIND consumes | `pfm-data/<group>/` |
| `all` | all three, in dependency order | everything |
| `custom` | pick individual steps | — |

```r
pfmRun(group = "psm-country-v5", stage = "all")            # data -> REMIND inputs
pfmRun(group = "psm-country-v5", stage = "downstream")     # from a finished sweep
pfmRun(group = "psm-country-v5", stage = "remind")         # export only
pfmRun(group = "psm-country-v5", stage = "all", dryRun = TRUE)   # plan, run nothing
```

On a cluster it submits with `sbatch` by default (`cluster = "auto"` detects SLURM);
`cluster = "local"` runs in the current session.

## What is reused, and what is recomputed

Two caches sit **outside** the Run-Group and are shared by all of them:

- `<resultsDir>/models/` — fitted models, keyed by specification **and** panel hash
- `<resultsDir>/panels/` — the panels themselves, content-addressed

So a new Run-Group over an unchanged panel re-uses every fit it has seen before: the
sweep still enumerates specifications, but each one is a cache lookup rather than an
estimation. This is why a fresh group is usually far cheaper than the first one.

Indicative single-run timings (country resolution, ~2500 specifications):

```
sweep-psm            2306 s   <- dominated by first-time fits; near-instant when cached
projection            276 s
selection-bootstrap   199 s
psm-coupling-bound    100 s
psm-donor              10 s
frontier / temporal / speeds / iv / influence   4-16 s each
psm-remind-inputs       0 s
```

A cache lookup requires the **panel hash to match**. Rebuilding the panel — new source
data, a changed mapping — produces a new hash and therefore a full re-estimation. That
is correct: those are different fits.

## Stale artifacts, and how to avoid trusting them

`resume = TRUE` skips a step when its artifact exists. That is a good answer to *did
this finish?* and a bad answer to *is this still valid?* A Run-Group carried across a
code change, a panel rebuild or a new gdx keeps artifacts that look complete and are
wrong.

This is not hypothetical: a projection covering 33 countries once sat beside a model
fitted on 48, and nothing complained, because the file existed.

Delete before rebuilding whenever the inputs moved underneath the group:

```r
pfmRun(group = "psm-country-v4", stage = "downstream", clean = "steps")
pfmRun(group = "psm-country-v4", stage = "all",        clean = "group")
```

- `clean = "steps"` — remove what the steps about to run write
- `clean = "group"` — remove every step artifact in the group
- `clean` always shows what it will delete and disables `resume` (deleting a file and
  then skipping the step for want of that file is worse than either alone)

Neither ever touches `models/` or `panels/`: those are content-addressed, shared, and
clearing them turns a short re-run into a multi-hour one. To force re-estimation of a
specific fit use `forceRefit`, not deletion.

Inspect without acting:

```r
psmStepArtifacts()                                  # step -> artifacts it writes
psmCleanSteps("psm-country-v4", "psm-projection", dryRun = TRUE)
```

### When to clean

| you changed | do |
|---|---|
| pfm source code | reinstall, then `clean = "steps"` for affected steps |
| the panel / source data | new hash, so nothing stale is reused — `clean` optional |
| the scenario gdx or registry | `clean = "steps"` on `psm-projection`, `psm-coupling-bound` |
| the deployed specification | `clean = "group"` |
| nothing | leave `clean = "none"` and let `resume` skip |

**Reinstall after editing the package.** `pfm-reports/start.R` and the steps load the
*installed* pfm, not your working tree — source edits do nothing until
`devtools::install("pfm")`. This has silently cost real debugging time.

## Handing the model to REMIND

`stage = "remind"` copies only what the coupling opens — six artifacts plus the one
panel named by `manifest.json:panel_hash` — into a self-contained folder, and refuses
to write a partial one:

```
pfm-data/<group>/
  selected-models-psm.yml   manifest.json   frontier.rds
  temporal-validation.rds   donor-assignment-band-{Bulk,Diffuse}.rds
  panels/panel_<hash>.rds
```

It then prints the lines to paste into your REMIND config:

```r
cfg$pfm$source <- "/path/to/pfm-data"
cfg$pfm$group  <- "psm-country-v4"   # omit if it is the only group there
```

and set `cm_taxCO2_regiDiff = 11` on the scenarios that should couple. REMIND's
`preparePFM.R` copies the folder into each run, so the run stays self-contained and
archivable.

At coupling time GAMS calls `pfm::iterativePFM()` from the run folder at each Nash
iteration from `c_pfmIter` onward. Nothing outside the run folder is read.

## Example: a scenario end to end

```r
options(pfm.resultsDir = "output", pfm.modelDir = "output")

# 1. estimate, project, bound — submits to SLURM on a cluster
pfmRun(group = "psm-country-v5", stage = "all",
       config = "config.yml", remindDir = "../pfm-data")

# 2. when the job finishes, export (a submitted job has not written its
#    inputs yet, so pfmRun tells you to run this separately)
pfmRun(group = "psm-country-v5", stage = "remind", remindDir = "../pfm-data")

# 3. check what the coupling will see
s <- readRDS("output/psm-country-v5/coupling/coupling-summary.rds")
s$thetaSweep
```

Then, in REMIND, set `cm_taxCO2_regiDiff = 11` and `c_pfmIter` on the scenario and
start it as usual. After the run:

```r
# gdx-authoritative check of what the coupling actually did
# pm_pfmConverged, p45_pfmCallCount, p45_pfmDelta, p45_pfmIterSeen
```

## A note on resolution

The PFM model is estimated and projected at **country** resolution, always.
Aggregation to REMIND regions (EU21, H12) happens only at the coupling boundary, in
`aggregateFeasibilityToRegions()`. The gdx supplies scenario drivers, which are
downscaled to countries; it does not set the model's resolution.
